priorReviewPolicy: P35 24 other cases are preserved, not re-adjudicated here

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: The Italian obliges baptized Christians always to profess the faith and observe Christ's and the Church's law; English 'is called to' softens the explicit obligation.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Use 'is obliged' / 'est tenu de' in a future bilingual candidate.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: Permanent renunciation of the devil, his works and pomps is directly present.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Keep as candidate, subject to Italian–English–French translation review.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: Sins and worldly maxims contrary to the Gospel are direct; the draft adds ritual-context commentary and the raw Italian answer includes the next section heading.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Separate contextual commentary and exclude the next section heading from quotation.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: Protection by a heavenly patron and imitation of the saint's example both occur explicitly.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Keep as candidate; resolve the digital transcription's typographic wording separately.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: Godparents answer at the font and guarantee Christian education particularly if parents fail; 'if necessary' weakens that condition.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Restore 'especially if the parents fail in that duty' in a future bilingual revision.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: The binding character of sponsors' promises is direct; 'not merely formal words' adds a reasonable explanatory contrast not written here.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Put the contrast into separate editorial commentary or omit it from source-attributed wording.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: Catholicity, good conduct and obedience to Church laws are direct; the note on present-day eligibility comes from later editorial context.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Keep source requirement and current canonical eligibility in separate labelled text.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: The source joins catechetical instruction, Christian life and exemplary conduct; 'above all by example' adds an unexpressed hierarchy.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Remove 'above all' in any source-limited paraphrase.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: The Italian says Confirmation gives the Holy Ghost, marks the soul with the character of a soldier of Christ, and makes 'perfect Christians'; 'greater maturity' is a modern interpretive gloss.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Retain the original character/perfection vocabulary, explaining historical usage separately.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: Strengthening in faith and perfecting virtues and gifts of Baptism are explicit; 'not an absence of faults' is a useful distinction but editorial.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Separate the explanatory qualification from source-attributed teaching.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: All seven gifts correspond to the Italian list without an obvious material omission.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Keep under normal bilingual and terminology review.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: Oil mixed with balsam and consecrated by the bishop on Holy Thursday is exactly the account given.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Keep with historical rite dating.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: The symbolism of strengthening/spreading grace and balsam's fragrance/preservation is represented in the paraphrase.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Check fine distinctions of virtue and corruption during specialist translation review.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: The bishop is named as ordinary minister; discussion of later faculties and contemporary discipline is not present in this answer.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Move post-1905 law/faculty caveat to the narrator.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: The forehead, shame and courage to profess the Christian name are all supported.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Keep as a bounded historical paraphrase.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: The text directs all to seek Confirmation and have dependants receive it.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Keep, with dependence terminology checked in French.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: Prayer, good works, Christ's law and freedom from human respect appear in the Italian.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Keep 'human respect' with a brief separate explanation if user needs it.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: Direction through words and example on the way of salvation and aid in spiritual combat are explicit.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Keep, subject to translation review.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: Suitability of age, Catholicity, Confirmation, religion and conduct are direct; present eligibility rules require independent current law.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Render historical list first, present-day canonical note separately.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: Conversion of bread/wine substance and whole Christ under both species for spiritual nourishment are expressed.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Keep, while reviewing exact theological terms across EN/FR.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: The identity of Eucharistic Christ with Jesus born of Mary and in heaven is direct.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Keep as historical catechetical answer.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: Christ's own declaration and the Church's teaching are the two stated reasons for belief.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Keep; avoid inventing an additional scriptural citation here.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: Wheat bread and vine wine are named; the draft's 'at the Last Supper' belongs to a different locus on institution, not to Q599 itself.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Omit Last-Supper detail or explicitly cite Q622 as a separate witness.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: The two words 'This is my Body' and 'This is my Blood' are direct; discussion of the entire Roman Canon belongs to an editorial liturgical note.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Keep the short catechetical form distinct from the complete liturgical formula.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: The source answers simply that the unconsecrated host is bread; the appended conversion comment is inferred from surrounding questions.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Keep 'It is bread' as source core; make expansion explicitly editorial.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: The postconsecration host is Christ's true Body under the species of bread.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Keep with careful EN/FR theological terminology.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: Before consecration the chalice contains wine with a few drops of water.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Keep as historical source description.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: After consecration, true Blood under wine species is directly stated.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Keep, translation review pending.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: The moment of conversion when the priest pronounces words of consecration at Mass is direct; calling them 'Christ's words' uses the immediately related Q600.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Keep the source's temporal claim; supply Q600 explicitly if expanding the formula.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: The original calls consecration a renewal through the priest of Christ's Last Supper miracle; 'in continuation of the mystery' is a less exact formulation.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Restore the word 'renewal' in an explicitly historical catechetical rendering.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: Christ's omnipotence is the direct explanation of the consecratory words' efficacy.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Keep with no causal interpolation.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: Only species remain is directly stated; 'not in substance' is context from adjacent conversion teaching.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Keep or cite Q596 for the substance contrast.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: Quantity, figure, colour and taste define species in the Italian; the claim that they remain after conversion comes from Q609.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Keep definitions and mark cross-question borrowing if retaining the extra clause.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: The miraculous persistence of species without substance is expressly attributed to God's omnipotence.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Keep in historical catechetical language.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: Whole living Christ is under both species, including Body, Blood, Soul and Divinity.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Keep, pending doctrinal-term EN/FR checks.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: The answer calls Christ living and immortal in heaven; 'risen Christ' is true theology but is not the wording of this specific answer.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Prefer 'living and immortal' in a strictly source-limited paraphrase.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: Christ remains in heaven while being in the sacrament; both locations are directly stated.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Keep without explaining spatial metaphysics beyond source.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: Christ's presence in all consecrated hosts is a direct one-sentence answer.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Keep in source-limited form.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: God's omnipotence directly explains presence in all hosts.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Keep; no need to invent a physical mechanism.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: Breaking the host divides the species, not Christ's Body; the distinction is direct.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Keep with precise Eucharistic terminology.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: The whole Body remains in every portion of the divided host.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Keep with theological language review.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: Adoration and carrying the sacrament to the sick are Q620's two reasons; 'Christ truly present' is supported by neighboring Q621/Q596.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Keep reasons in Q620; cite the other passage if expressly expanding Real Presence.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: The Italian grounds adoration in real and substantial presence; divine adoration is a correct doctrinal inference but not Q621's full wording, and raw extraction carries a following section heading.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Remove source-section furniture; mark explanatory inference as editor's.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: Institution at the Last Supper the evening before the Passion is direct.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Keep.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: New Law sacrifice, spiritual food, perpetual memorial and pledge of love/eternal life all occur explicitly.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Keep while preserving the source's three-part enumeration.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: Food and drink appearances are explained by spiritual nourishment; the draft captures the claim.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Keep.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: The original says the life of the soul is grace; the draft specifies 'sanctifying grace', an interpretive doctrinal specialization not quoted here.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Use 'grace' or support the more specific term with a separate theological source.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: The original says passions, especially concupiscence; 'disordered passions' is interpretive shorthand and the raw extract carries the next disposition section heading.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Keep the enumerated effects and remove section furniture; consider naming concupiscence.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: The source explicitly specifies modesty in the person and clothing in addition to preparation before and thanksgiving after Communion.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Restore outward conduct/dress in the bilingual historical wording.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: Meditation on the recipient and on Christ, plus the specified sequence of acts, is represented.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Check 'contrizione' as contrition rather than generic sorrow in the final translation.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: Acts of offering, thanksgiving and petition are direct, but the source emphasizes petitions for those for whom one is obliged to pray.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Preserve this duty-to-pray qualification rather than only generic 'others'.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: Recollection as possible, works of piety and fulfilment of one's state in life appear directly.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Keep.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: The distinction between sacramental Real Presence and grace is direct; the raw digital extraction includes the following section heading.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Keep the distinction, remove the heading from any quoted answer.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: The Italian defines sacrifice as offering a sensible thing to God and destroying it in some way; 'sacrificial change or destruction' may dilute the particular historical wording.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Prefer 'destroy it in some manner' in a historical-source translation; separate doctrinal definition from commentary.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: The sacrifice of the New Law is called Holy Mass.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Keep.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: The sacrifice of Christ's Body and Blood offered under species of bread and wine in memorial of Calvary is direct.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Keep.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: The distinction between bloody offering on the Cross and bloodless Mass is direct; 'without a new shedding' adds the word new, which is editorial.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Prefer the source's 'without shedding blood' when attributing to Q656.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: The distinct sacramental species represent shedding of Christ's Blood, while whole living Christ remains present under both.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Keep this two-sided account together.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: Calvary's unique redemptive merits and the Mass applying them are direct; 'does not add a second independent redemption' is an explanatory inference.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: The four ends and their definitions correspond to latreutic, Eucharistic, propitiatory and impetratory.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: Christ as first/principal offerer and priest as minister acting in His name are direct.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: Christ instituted Mass with the Eucharist and commanded memorial of His Passion.
assessments.nextEvidenceOrCorrectionAction: Keep.

assessments.sourceToDraftFinding: Mass is offered to God alone.
